item.title: Derived products and completion defects of inverse limits
item.description: arXiv:2610.34022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute derived products and inverse limits in Grothendieck categories by exact coresolutions. For the product of $r$ doubled affine lines over $B[s]$, where $B$ is any nonzero commutative ring,the exact dimensions of products, epimorphic countable limits, and arbitrary countable limits are $r$, $r$, and $r+1$. We identify the top derived functors for every $B$-module of coefficients. Both obstruction modules contain the countable reduced product as a natural $B$-module direct summand, and a formal-series map relates them by an explicit cokernel sequence. A relative cofree coresolution gives degree shifts over an arbitrary Grothendieck category and computes the localization defect for arbitrary locally nilpotent diagrams. We also construct transfinite scalar extensions preserving a prescribed kernel and its derived limit;these give nonzero completion defects beyond any fixed ordinal.The general epimorphic top-degree vanishing question is not settled by these constructions.
item.dc:creator: Rui Zeng (Sichuan Normal University), Guocheng Dai (Sichuan Normal University)

item.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Hao Guo, Chenxi Wang, Guoliang Yu

item.title: Higher Spherical Scissors Congruence II: Comodules
item.description: arXiv:2610.35567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define the higher Dehn invariant on the Euclidean, hyperbolic, and spherical variants of scissors congruence $K$-theory, and prove that it makes these spectra into comodules over the spectral Sah algebra. This allows us to make the first formulation of the conjecture that the higher volume and Dehn invariants are jointly injective.
item.dc:creator: Inbar Klang, Josefien Kuijper, Cary Malkiewich, David Mehrle, Thor Wittich

item.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.34898v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which every positive residue characteristic of $S$ is invertible. We prove that Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients is canonically equivalent to modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The comparison identifies the corresponding commutative coefficient algebras and is compatible with arbitrary pullback. The theorem applies to singular and nonreduced schemes, including mixed-characteristic bases, and requires no excellence or finite-type hypothesis. Its special cases include rational coefficients over arbitrary bases, arbitrary coefficients over $\mathbb Q$-schemes, and $\mathbb Z[1/p]$-algebra coefficients over $\mathbb Z_{(p)}$-schemes. The proof establishes base change for finite-cycle spectra using permutation quotients, families of cycles, and arithmetic power homotopies, then passes to general bases by universal homeomorphism invariance and continuity.
item.dc:creator: Bo Zhang

item.title: A cohomology operation encoding the octahedral axiom
item.description: arXiv:2610.35232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a new secondary cohomology operation, the naturality defect product, associated with a graded natural transformation between the cohomology functors of two differential graded functors, and study its main properties. We then prove that a pretriangulated category satisfies the octahedral axiom if and only if the naturality defect product associated with the natural isomorphism given by a theorem of Heller vanishes on the homotopy category of acyclic complexes over it. This characterization extends immediately to n-angulated categories. As an application, we exhibit non-vanishing instances for the recently found examples of pretriangulated categories which are not triangulated. Finally, we show that horizontal composition of these natural isomorphisms preserves n-angulated structures, and we use it to obtain, from each of these examples and for every r >= 1, a pre-3r-angulated category which is not 3r-angulated.
item.dc:creator: Javier D\'iaz Cabrera, Fernando Muro

item.title: On explicit formulas for Grassmannian polylogarithms and Gelfand-MacPherson forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.35754v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We answer a question of Goncharov by showing that his Grassmannian $n$-logarithm can be recovered by integrating the Borel invariant form on the symmetric space $\mathrm{SL}_{n}(\mathbf{C})/\mathrm{SU}(n)$ over a naturally defined ideal simplex. As corollaries, we recover the finiteness of primitive canonical integrals of Brown and the evaluation for wheel graphs of Brown and Schnetz. We also compute explicitly the Gelfand-MacPherson forms for powers of the first Pontryagin class and give a general integral formula for the Gelfand-MacPherson forms associated to each component of the Pontryagin character.
item.dc:creator: Juan Diego Rojas

item.title: The algebraic K-theory of $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$
item.description: arXiv:2606.21421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute via trace methods the higher algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$, as well as the related groups $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, and $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $k$ is a finite field of characteristic $p$ and $q=p^r$. At the core of the computation is the algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring of the Sylow $p$-subgroup, $k[C_p^r]$, which we determine via a theorem of L\"uck--Reich--Rognes--Varisco on cyclic assembly for topological cyclic homology. In the process, we reprove the cyclic assembly result in the language of Nikolaus--Scholze, analyse assembly for smaller families of subgroups, and develop further tools for computing topological cyclic homology of group rings.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Moselle

item.title: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension of complex varieties
item.description: arXiv:2312.06930v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Lichtenbaum-Quillen conjecture for smooth complex varieties states that algebraic and topological K-theory with finite coefficients become isomorphic in high degrees. We define the "Lichtenbaum-Quillen dimension" of a variety in terms of the point where this happens, show that it is surprisingly computable, and analyze many examples. It gives an obstruction to rationality, but one that turns out to be weaker than unramified cohomology and some related birational invariants defined by Colliot-Th\'el\`ene and Voisin using Bloch-Ogus theory. Because it is compatible with semi-orthogonal decompositions, however, it allows us to prove some new cases of the integral Hodge conjecture using homological projective duality, and to compute the higher algebraic K-theory of the Kuznetsov components of the derived categories of some Fano varieties.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Addington, Elden Elmanto

item.title: BV rigidity in the string topology of compact Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.04164v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected compact Lie group and $R$ a commutative ring over which $H_*(G;R)$ is an exterior algebra on odd primitive generators. We prove a rigidity theorem: the Batalin-Vilkovisky (BV) algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ of Chas and Sullivan on the homology of the free loop space is that of the product of odd spheres with the classical exponents of $G$, tensored with the group ring of the torsion of $\pi_1(G)$. Conversely, over an integral domain the graded algebra $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$ already determines the exponents and the group ring, hence the BV algebra. The isomorphism with the product of spheres is algebraic: for $\mathrm{Sp}(n)$, $n\geq2$, and $\mathrm{SU}(n)$, $n\geq3$, no map of spaces induces it over $\mathbb{Z}$. If moreover $G$ is simply connected, then $\mathbb{H}_*(LG;R)$, as a BV algebra, is the Hochschild cohomology of $H^*(G;R)$ with the BV operator induced by Poincar\'e duality.
item.dc:creator: Mukilraj K (Indian Institute of Science Education,Research Kolkata, India)
